title: Second cohomology of a generic extension on an affine curve
statement:
Let $C/k$ be a smooth integral affine
connected curve over algebraically closed $k$
and $\eta:\operatorname{Spec}k(C)\to C$ its
generic point.
For every torsion etale sheaf
$M$ on $\operatorname{Spec}k(C)$, one has
$H^2(C,\eta_*M)=0$, with
etale cohomology.

proof.text:
First let $M$ be finite $\ell$-primary. Use
[lem-exc-field-discrete-modules], [lem-sc-sylow-module-filtration]
to choose a finite separable extension $K'/K$, $K=k(C)$,
of degree $d$ prime to $\ell$, such that $M'=M|_{K'}$
has a filtration by trivial $\mathbf F_\ell$-modules.
Write $a:\eta'=\operatorname{Spec}K'\to\eta$.
The finite etale trace on the field is the sum over the $d$
geometric points of its fibre. The unit and this sum give

$$
M\longrightarrow a_*a^*M\longrightarrow M
$$

with composite $d\,\mathrm{id}$. Multiplication by $d$ is
invertible, so this is a splitting after rescaling the sum.
No trace for a ramified morphism is being asserted.

Use [lem-sc-finite-extension-affine-model] to obtain
$h:C'\to C$ and the generic point map $b:\eta'\to C'$.
The equality $h b=\eta a$ gives
$\eta_*a_*M'=h_*b_*M'$. Applying $\eta_*$ to the splitting
makes $\eta_*M$ a direct summand of this sheaf.
Finite direct image is exact by
[lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact], and since $b_*M'$ is
killed by the exponent of $M'$, hence torsion,
[lem-fd-finite-pushforward-cohomology] gives
$H^2(C,h_*b_*M')\cong H^2(C',b_*M')$; a direct summand of a zero
group is zero, so it remains to prove $H^2(C',b_*M')=0$.

For a filtration step $0\to M_1\to M_2\to M_3\to0$, put
$G_i=b_*M_i$ and $I=\operatorname{im}(G_2\to G_3)$.
Although $b_*$ need not be exact, [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-left-exact]
gives $0\to G_1\to G_2\to I\to0$. The sheaf $G_3/I$ has zero
generic restriction: for a geometric point $\bar\xi$ over the generic
point of $C'$ the strict henselization is $\operatorname{Spec}K'^{\rm sep}$,
so [lem-weil-pbc-unrestricted-strict-henselization-stalk] (for the affine,
hence quasi-compact quasi-separated, morphism $b$ and $q=0$) identifies
$(b_*M_i)_{\bar\xi}$ with the stalk $(M_i)_{\bar\xi}$, i.e. the counit
$b^{-1}b_*M_i\to M_i$ is an isomorphism; as $b^{-1}$ is exact
[prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], $b^{-1}(G_3/I)$ is the cokernel
of the surjection $M_2\to M_3$, hence zero. It is torsion, being killed by
the exponent of $M_3$. By [lem-sc-zero-generic-acyclic],
$H^2(C',I)\simeq H^2(C',G_3)$. Applying the long exact
sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] to the two
short exact sequences shows that vanishing for $G_1$ and $G_3$
implies vanishing for $G_2$. For a trivial quotient,
[lem-fin-normal-generic-constant] gives $b_*\mathbf F_\ell=\mathbf F_\ell$
(the smooth curve $C'$ is Noetherian, normal and integral).
The base case is [lem-sc-affine-constant-second]. Induction through
the filtration proves the finite case.

A general torsion $G_K$-module is the directed union of finite
stable submodules: each orbit is finite by continuity, and a
finite set of torsion generators generates a finite group.
Separate the finitely many primary parts of each finite module.
On a quasi-compact etale test curve the generic fibre is a finite
disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions, so
sections of $\eta_*$ are finite products of invariant groups;
invariants commute with directed unions because membership is
checked elementwise. Thus $\eta_*$ commutes with this directed
union. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit] proves
the assertion for the union.
